A1_1.evidence: Open, free, universally implementable protocol (HTTPS/DOI resolution to Zenodo, public API returns the record without credentials); the code itself is for an open-source runtime - 'implemented in the open-source computing environment R (R Core Team, 2021)'.

A1_2.evidence: v2.1 open case: fully open deposit ('access_right': 'open') with no access control existing or warranted, so the authentication requirement is vacuously met; no restricted or embargoed state is recorded.

A2.evidence: Row 2 Zenodo persistence entitlement (tombstone on withdrawal retaining DOI and URL; metadata always publicly accessible; retention for the repository's lifetime), applicable because rung (i) establishes the code is deposited on Zenodo rather than GitHub/GitLab (Row 5, which carries no persistence entitlement).

F1.evidence: The paper's own analysis scripts (principal code artefact) are deposited under a DOI: 'Dedicated R code and complete data tables are reported in Supplementary Information S2 and S3 ... F3.evidence: Record carries its own identifier: 'identifier_in_metadata': true with 'doi': '10.5281/zenodo.10623550' and 'record_id_on_service': 10623550 (later version 10.5281/zenodo.10801706 likewise).

F4.evidence: Indexed in searchable registries: DataCite returned the record with 'state': 'findable' and the Zenodo API resolved it (HTTP 200) - Zenodo/DataCite indexing confirmed at the granting services.

I1.evidence: Code is written in a formal, open, broadly shared language rather than a proprietary or binary form: 'We use the skipgram approach and PMI measure, implemented in the open-source computing environment R (R Core Team, 2021)' and 'All analyses were performed in the open-source R programming environment (v.4.2.2 ...), using the Quanteda package (Benoit et al., 2018)'.

I2.evidence: No FAIR software vocabulary applied. I3.evidence: Per the v2.1 aggregation rule, third-party dependencies enter scoring through citation quality: the paper types the relation and supplies a PID for the principal dependency - 'using the Quanteda package (Benoit et al., 2018)', cited as 'quanteda: an R package for the quantitative analysis of textual data. This is the PID-bearing 'uses software [DOI]' reference that the equivalent data-side citation (Plonka 2003, no DOI) lacks.

R1.evidence: The code is described by a plurality of relevant attributes sufficient to understand and rerun it: purpose and algorithm ('k-skip-n-gram (skipgram) models and associated pointwise mutual information (PMI) measures'), the explicit expected-frequency and PMI formulae, the parameter choice and its justification ('the maximum number of individual motifs on a single object is 15, and the k value for all generated skipgrams is thus set to 13'), the analysis levels ('results at the level of 2-, 3-, and 4-grams'), and the environment/dependency pair (R v4.2.2, quanteda). A deposit-side README could not be inspected (supplement withheld).

R1_1.evidence: The deposit containing the code carries an identified licence: pack 'licences': ['cc-by-4.0'] at both the Zenodo and DataCite views of 10.5281/zenodo.10623550, 'licence_conflicts': []. The paper asserts no different code licence, so no most-restrictive same-artefact conflict arises (CC-BY is a permissive though non-software-specific licence).

R1_2.evidence: Provenance of the code artefact is documented: authorship and date via the deposit record (publisher Zenodo, publication_year 2024) and CRediT ('Lasse Lukas Platz Herskind: ... Methodology, Investigation, Formal analysis, Data curation'), plus the full processing chain the code implements (digitisation, transformation to sentence-imitating strings, skipgram generation at k=13, PMI computation) and the exact software environment (R v4.2.2 with quanteda).

R1_3.evidence: R1.3 route (a), generic metadata schema: the code is distributed in a Zenodo deposit carrying a DataCite metadata record (pack DataCite endpoint resolved, state 'findable'). No code-specific standard is evidenced - no CITATION.cff, CodeMeta, package structure, or community review (not CRAN/JOSS/rOpenSci), and the record is typed 'Dataset' rather than Software - so the score rests solely on the generic-schema route.

A2.evidence: Rung-(ii) Row 2 Zenodo entitlement: tombstone page on withdrawal with DOI and URL retained, records preserved on retraction, retention for the lifetime of the repository, and metadata always publicly accessible; rung (i) confirms the artefacts are Zenodo deposits with resolvable DataCite records.

F2.evidence: Independent artefact-level metadata record exists (instrument's F1 note glosses F2 as 'independent metadata record'): pack records 'metadata_record': true for both the DataCite and the Zenodo API views, with non-null mandatory values (publisher 'Zenodo', publication_year 2024, resource_type 'Dataset'), corroborating the Row 2 Zenodo/Row 1 DataCite entitlement to a DataCite metadata record rather than a null-coded shell.

F3.evidence: The identifier is carried in the record itself: pack fields 'identifier_in_metadata': true and 'doi': '10.5281/zenodo.10623550' (likewise 'doi': '10.5281/zenodo.10801706'), plus 'record_id_on_service': 10623550 in the Zenodo view.

F4.evidence: Registry indexing confirmed at the granting service: the DataCite API returned the record with 'state': 'findable' (HTTP 200) for both deposits, and the Zenodo API resolved both records - Zenodo/DataCite are instrument-listed searchable registries.

I1.evidence: Rung-(i) paper text establishes a structured, machine-parseable representation: Plonka's scheme 'was transcribed as binary data in the form of presence/absence coding of motif types (named A1, A2, etc.) on each individual artefact', these data 'consist of numerous categorical variables', and 'All analyses were performed in the open-source R programming environment (v.4.2.2 ...), using the Quanteda package', with 'All code and data ... available here: https://zenodo.org/records/10623550' - i.e. the deposited tables are the machine-readable inputs the deposited R code consumes. File-level formats could not be inspected directly (supplement withheld; pack carries no format field), so this rests on the paper's own description.

I2.evidence: No FAIR vocabulary is used. Motif terms are Plonka's (2003, pp. 315-325) in-house alphanumeric typology ('named A1, A2, etc.'), transcribed by the authors; chronological units are free-text culture-complex labels ('Maglemose', 'Kongemose', 'Ertebolle') with no PeriodO, Getty AAT, CIDOC-CRM or ARIADNEplus URIs. Looked for vocabulary/ontology citations in Methods and for vocabulary fields in the pack - none present.

I3.evidence: No qualified (PID-typed) references from the dataset to other resources. The dataset's derivation source is cited without any persistent identifier ('Plonka, T., 2003. The portable art of mesolithic europe ... Wydawn. Uniw. Wroclawskiego, Wroclaw' - no DOI in the reference list), and the pack records no relatedIdentifiers for either Zenodo record; the only PID relation captured is the internal Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.10623549 (self-versioning), which is not a reference to another resource. Row 2 grants no relatedIdentifier entitlement.

R1.evidence: Plurality of relevant attributes documented: the data 'consist of numerous categorical variables corresponding to the characteristics of each ornamented object and associated metadata such as location, quality of contextual information, and original source', supplemented by artefact class and culture-historical attribution (Fig. 2, Table 3), and the paper states 'We do include pertinent metadata such as artefact classes, chronology, and spatial distribution'.

R1_1.evidence: Licence identified, not merely a mandatory field: pack records 'licences': ['cc-by-4.0'] for both the DataCite and Zenodo views of both deposits, with 'licence_conflicts': []. The paper is silent on a dataset licence, so per the R1.1 rule the service-recorded licence governs; the Zenodo default-licence footnote makes a default-valued CC-BY fully operative. The article's own CC BY 4.0 is consistent, so no most-restrictive conflict arises.

R1_2.evidence: Detailed provenance of dataset creation and transformation is documented: source and extraction ('the case study ... rests on the comprehensive catalogue ... compiled by Plonka (2003). From this analogue compilation, the South Scandinavian data were manually extracted and digitised'), coding scheme and its page range (2003, pp. 315-325), the transformation step ('transformed from presence/absence coding into a sentence-imitating structure ... in arbitrary, alphabetical order'), parameters (k set to 13; the explicit expected-frequency and PMI formulae), and processing environment (R v4.2.2, quanteda), with the generating code deposited alongside the data.

R1_3.evidence: R1.3 route (a), generic metadata schemas: the deposits carry DataCite metadata records (pack DataCite endpoint resolved, HTTP 200, state 'findable', publisher/publicationYear/resourceType populated), which is the Row 2 Zenodo entitlement. No domain route applies - no ARIADNEplus/CIDOC-CRM/Dublin Core domain profile is evidenced, and the deposit is not in an accredited domain repository (not ADS/DANS/tDAR). Methodological content (skipgram, PMI) is expressly excluded from R1.3.
